description: Driven by a deep passion for space exploration and engineering, we are Software Engineering innovators building AI/RAG pipelines and full-stack interfaces. Our motto is turning raw orbital science into actionable intelligence. Tackling "Flame in Freefall," we are engineering a high-precision, AI-powered dashboard to decode NASA’s microgravity combustion data—redefining fire safety for humanity’s return to the Moon and Mars.
summary:
FLAMESCOPE is an AI-powered telemetry, fire-risk analysis, and interactive visualization platform built on NASA’s Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) combustion datasets (including FLEX, BASS-II, SAFFIRE-III, and SAME-R).
Microgravity alters combustion by eliminating buoyancy-driven convection, making fire behavior in spacecraft and lunar habitats difficult to interpret from raw experimental tables alone. FLAMESCOPE addresses this challenge through a three-tier architecture: a Spring Boot and PostgreSQL/pgvector data engine structuring 514 verified experimental runs with strict unit-quality provenance, an interactive React dashboard featuring ECharts telemetry comparisons, scenario risk modeling, and Three.js 3D microgravity flame simulations, and a local Ollama-driven RAG assistant (qwen2.5:3b and qwen3-embedding:0.6b) that enforces cell-level citation validation to eliminate scientific hallucinations.
By transforming fragmented NASA PSI records into traceable, visual, and verifiable insights, FLAMESCOPE helps engineers assess material flammability, design safer crewed habitats, and translate microgravity combustion findings into next-generation fire suppression systems on Earth.
details:
FLAMESCOPE (developed by Team PYROSPHERE) is an interactive telemetry, fire-risk assessment, and scientific evidence platform built on NASA’s Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) combustion datasets—covering 514 structured experimental and sample records across FLEX (PSI-69), BASS-II (PSI-25), SAME-R (PSI-101), and SAFFIRE-III (PSI-100), alongside a cataloged inventory of 9 PSI combustion investigations.

The platform operates through a three-tier architecture:

  1. Verified Data & Backend Engine: An idempotent Python ETL pipeline ingests raw NASA CSV and XLSX tables with SHA-256 hash verification, row-level fingerprinting, and strict preservation of original qualifiers (EXACT, CHANGING, GREATER_THAN, LESS_THAN, MISSING) without altering raw values. A Java Spring Boot REST API backed by PostgreSQL 16 and Flyway serves paginated experiment catalogs, full test provenance (DOIs, original tables, and unit-quality flags), and deterministic multi-experiment comparisons.
  2. Interactive Telemetry & 3D Visualization Dashboard: A React web application enables researchers to explore experiments, compare burn times, extinction diameters, and gas concentrations via ECharts telemetry charts, run scenario-based fire risk assessments, and inspect interactive Three.js 3D microgravity flame simulations illustrating how eliminating buoyancy transforms teardrop Earth flames into spherical, soot-free microgravity flames under varying oxygen and airflow conditions.
  3. Hallucination-Guarded RAG Assistant: A dedicated FastAPI service indexed over 643 hash-verified evidence rows in pgvector answers natural-language questions using local Ollama models (qwen3-embedding:0.6b and qwen2.5:3b). Every response enforces cell-level schema validation and inline citations ([S1]), automatically routing mathematical queries to deterministic SQL/backend analysis (STRUCTURED_ANALYSIS_REQUIRED) and declining unsupported extrapolations (INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE).

Benefits & Intended Impact Microgravity eliminates buoyancy-driven convection, fundamentally altering flame ignition, spread, and extinction in ways that are difficult to interpret from fragmented spreadsheets alone. FLAMESCOPE turns raw NASA PSI tables into traceable, visual, and verifiable engineering insights. For space exploration, it helps mission planners and spacecraft engineers evaluate material flammability and fire-suppression needs for crewed spacecraft and future lunar habitats—where elevated oxygen levels and partial gravity increase fire hazards. On Earth, making microgravity combustion findings accessible supports the development of cleaner combustion models, fine water-mist fire extinguishers, advanced smoke detection, and improved firefighter protective gear.

Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used

  • Languages: Java 21, Python 3.12+, JavaScript (ES6+/JSX), SQL, HTML5, CSS3.
  • Backend & Database: Spring Boot, Flyway, PostgreSQL 16 with pgvector, FastAPI, Pydantic, psycopg, Docker & Docker Compose.
  • Frontend & Visualization: React 19, Vite, ECharts, Three.js.
  • Local AI & Retrieval: Ollama (qwen2.5:3b for structured cell extraction and qwen3-embedding:0.6b for 1024-dimensional embeddings).
  • Environment & Testing: Git/GitHub, Maven, Node.js, Python unittest, automated browser/API test suites, developed on Windows 11 with WSL2 Ubuntu Linux.

Creativity & Key Factors Considered

  • Scientific Integrity Over Unconstrained AI: Rather than allowing a language model to generate free-form prose or guess missing numbers, we built a fail-closed validation architecture. Ambiguous source columns (such as FLEX’s "Burning rate; mm") are explicitly flagged as REQUIRES_REVIEW and excluded from automated unit conversions or arithmetic, and blank cells are never imputed as zero.
  • Strict Source Provenance: CSV files and multi-sheet XLSX workbooks retain separate worksheet, row, and cell provenance so no original NASA record is overwritten or merged improperly.
  • Offline & Reproducible Deployment: By containerizing PostgreSQL/pgvector and running Ollama models locally, FLAMESCOPE runs completely offline without external API keys or cloud dependencies.
